title: API quota entropy lab notes
content:
Context / motivation:
- Intermittent 401/429 cluster seen over last two weeks for a subset of customers. Not full outage, but client stacks reporting cascading 429s after ephemeral key rotation and when burst traffic hits a specific owner key.
- This doc is a live scratchpad: experiments run locally and on staging, short commands, quick dumps of response bodies and rough hypothesis ranking.

Observed symptoms (summary):
- 401 surfaced as: {"error":{"type":"authentication_error","message":"Invalid API key"}} returned immediately.
- 429 surfaced with two flavors: 429a (standard rate limit) with Retry-After: <n> header and body hinting rate_window; 429b (quota-exceeded) with body: {"error":"Quota exceeded for account"}.
- In several cases, clients received 401 then ~200ms later a batch of 429s. Timing suggests a short-lived state change (key revocation/rotation) that triggers fallback clients to retry aggressively.
- Correlated spikes in serving logs with dedicated-pool autoscaling events (scale up/down) in region-us-west2 on 2024-11-01 03:12-03:18 UTC.

Commands / quick reproductions tried (staging):
1) Simple curl showing immediate 401 for rotated key:
   curl -s -D - -o /dev/null \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-ROTATED" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -X POST https://staging-api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"input":"hello"}'
   -> HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
      WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="redwood"
      {"error":{"type":"authentication_error","message":"Invalid API key"}}

2) Load test that produced 429 pattern (k6 local run):
   k6 run --vus 50 --duration 2m load-test-script.js
   Observed: initial 20s steady 200s, then incremental 429s between 00:21 - 00:35. Retry-After header values were inconsistent (sometimes absent).

3) Rapid rotate test (simulate ephemeral rotation):
   - Rotate key via staging admin API every 30s while firing 10 concurrent connections.
   - Results: around 10-15% of requests hit 401 during rotation window; following 401 burst, retries (no jitter) produced 429 flood for same owner id.

4) Direct calls to token-validation service to see propagation lag:
   time curl -s -X GET "https://staging-internal.redwood.ai/kv/keys/sk-live-XXXXX/status" \
        -H "Authorization: Bearer internal-microkey"
   -> observed 200 with last_seen_rev: 2024-11-02T03:17:02Z while public requests already returning 401 at 03:16:58Z. Suggests ~4s window where edge cached an old key state.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Ephemeral key rotation + aggressive client retry leads to transient 401 followed by 429s because of per-key rate limiter being hit by throttled backfill traffic. (HIGH)
2) Rate-limiter bucket granularity is per API key AND per account; when key is rotated, old key requests get remapped to the same account bucket but with additional burst metadata causing bucket mis-accounting. (MEDIUM)
3) Edge cache TTL for key validation is longer than internal key revocation TTL -> short window where behavior is inconsistent between edge and control plane, causing mixed 401/200 responses. (MEDIUM)
4) Autoscaling events cause small perf blips that increase request latency and pile up on retries, which in aggregate exceeds token-per-second windows, causing 429s. (LOW-MED)
5) A separate quota enforcement pathway (billing quota) kicks in and returns 429b without Retry-After; these are getting conflated with rate-limit 429a. (MEDIUM)

Things tried as mitigation in staging:
- Introduced exponential backoff + full jitter in client harness -> reduced 429 tail by ~35%.
- Increased key-validation cache TTL in edge from 2s -> 6s for one experiment (made 401 windows longer but reduced 401->429 cascade). Not ideal.
- Swapped per-key bucket to per-account bucket in a local mock -> produced more even distribution but masked some bad clients (not a fix).

Quick artifact of timing (rough heatmap) - counts of 401/429 per 30s bucket during rotate test (sample):
- Time (UTC)        | 401 | 429
- 03:16:30 - 03:17:00 | 12  | 3
- 03:17:00 - 03:17:30 | 48  | 110
- 03:17:30 - 03:18:00 | 8   | 230
- 03:18:00 - 03:18:30 | 0   | 42
Notes: big spike in 429 immediately after rotation; 401 peak slightly earlier.

Logs / places to check next:
- edge-auth-proxy logs (filtered by owner_id) around rotation timestamps
- rate-limiter service metrics (token-buckets per owner and per-key) 1s granularity
- keystore changefeed / pubsub delivery times (control plane -> edge)
- dedicated-pool scaling events correlation (cloud provider events)
- client SDK logs (retry loop timing) from a few anonymized customers

Repro plan for next 48h (staging):
1) Controlled rotation + staggered clients: 3 experiments where rotation interval = [30s, 60s, 120s]; clients use backoff strategies: none, fixed jitter, full jitter. Measure 401->429 cascade counts.
2) Add a bypass in edge for validation (force consult control plane on every (small sample) request) to measure true propagation lag.
3) Run dedicated rate-limiter telemetry capture with sample rate 1:10 for owner buckets to get token-bucket states and transient exhaust reasons.
4) Produce a minimal reproducible case for infra (k8s svc + autoscaler + edge) to hand off to platform team.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Is there an SLA on key revocation propagation we agreed on? (check confluence)
- Should we introduce a short grace period after rotation where old key is accepted for 1s to drain inflight requests? Pros/cons?
- Can billing quota and rate limiter return distinct error codes to avoid conflation in client handling?
- Can we add structured debug headers to responses to indicate which subsystem returned 429 (rate-limit vs quota vs throttling)?

Notes to self: keep this doc focused on experimental outcomes, move final recommendations into a short one-pager for infra and sdk teams.

Experiment logs (raw snippets):
- 2024-11-02T03:17:01.124Z REQUEST id=abc123 owner=acct-77 key=sk-live-OLD -> 401 {"error":{"type":"authentication_error","message":"Invalid API key"}}
- 2024-11-02T03:17:01.520Z REQUEST id=abc124 owner=acct-77 key=sk-live-OLD -> 429 {"error":"rate limit exceeded"} Retry-After: 1
- 2024-11-02T03:17:10.902Z REQUEST id=abc333 owner=acct-77 key=sk-live-NEW -> 200 {"id":"resp-xyz","output":"hi"}

Slack refs: #sre-api-debugging thread 2024-11-02 "rotation spike" (see pinned messages).
Jira: INF-1423 covers billing/quota change from Oct. Might overlap with 429b behavior.

Next update: after running staged experiments on 2024-11-09.

— maya
